messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — elevated 5xx / timeouts observed from infer-runtime cluster eu-west-1. Spike started ~4023456786. Affected service: model-runner pool (quantized models). Pager assigned to Jess (oncall). Trace: https://internal.redwood/traces/4023456789 :rotating_light:

Jess (oncall): On it. Pulling up dashboards and logs. @Liam can you join? I'm seeing a correlated GPU memory bump then segfaults on a small subset of pods.

Liam (eng-runtime): Joining. Looking at runner-0a3 logs, repeated OOM followed by SIGSEGV in attention kernel (quantized). grabbing core dump and nvlogs now.

Maya (SRE): I can start mitigation from the routing side. Recommend immediate fallback to smaller-model-variant and draining the crashing nodes. Will prepare the routing patch.

Jess (oncall): Applying fallback route now — switching traffic for model:embed-cpu-heavy -> model:embed-small-fallback. Command (applying):

```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap routing-config --type='json' -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/routes/embed-cpu-heavy","value":"embed-small-fallback"}]'
```

deploy-bot: Hosted routing rollout started for embed-cpu-heavy -> embed-small-fallback. Progress: 10% -> 35% -> 70% (updates every 30s).

Liam (eng-runtime): Core dump analysis snippet (gdb):

```
#0  0x7f2a1b2c in q_attn_cuda::launch_kernel() at q_attn_cuda.c:213
#1  0x7f2a1c3d in model_runner::run_attention() at runner.cc:487
#2  0x7f2a1d4e in inference::execute_step() at engine.cc:1210
```

Memory metrics show a sharp allocation ~2s before crash (~11GB spike on a 16GB GPU). Suspect kernel mis-size on large sequence lengths after quantization path.

Tom (Infra): Scaling up eu-west-1 pool by +4 GPUs to reduce queue pressure and isolate faulty pods. Marking pods runner-0a3 and runner-0a4 as unschedulable and cordoning them for debug.

Rita (Support): Notifying impacted accounts. Current customer-facing summary: "We observed elevated errors for inference requests to certain models in eu-west-1. We’ve applied a temporary fallback and are rolling a runtime patch; we’ll follow up with details." Logged 3 P1 customer tickets and 7 P2s.

Jess (oncall): Fallback routing at 100%. Error rate from dashboards: dropped from ~12% -> 1.3% overall. Latency improved but long-context (>2k tokens) requests still produce sporadic 502s/timeouts.

Liam (eng-runtime): Pushed hotpatch guard to kernel launch (validate sizes, fail gracefully if allocation > threshold) — PR: https://internal.redwood/pull/1234. Deploying to canary (runner-canary-1).

deploy-bot: Hotpatch applied to canary. Health checks: ok. No crashes in canary for 9m. Rolling to 25% traffic.

Maya (SRE): Enabled verbose kvcache and allocator tracing on canary to capture growth pattern. If stable for 30m, we'll promote. Also turning on increased sampling for core dumps (minidump) to capture any future anomalies.

Jess (oncall): Monitoring. Current state: mitigated (fallback + scale + hotpatch canary). Pager will be closed but incident remains in "monitoring" for 60m.

Liam (eng-runtime): Preliminary root cause hypothesis: quantized attention kernel miscomputes allocation size for certain sequence-length/attention-window combinations -> memory overcommit -> kernel OOM -> segfault. Next steps: reproduce with unit test, add bounds checks in kernel, verify on multi-GPU.

Rita (Support): Customers updated. One enterprise customer reported retries exhausted on a long-running batch; we provided workaround and credit.

Jess (oncall): Summary for incident record: impact window ~4023456786 -> 4023456802 (~1.6m active spike, mitigation completed ~4023456802), peak error rate ~12%, primary symptom: 5xx / timeouts from model-runner pods in eu-west-1, mitigations: fallback routing, scale up, cordon/crash isolation, runtime hotpatch canary. Action items: (1) eng-runtime to produce PR with kernel fix and test (Liam) (2) SRE to run canary for 30m then promote if stable (Maya) (3) Support to close customer tickets after follow-ups (Rita) (4) Postmortem doc and RCA (Jess)

Jess (oncall): Closing pager. If any new crashes appear reopen immediately or @pager. :thumbsup:
